{{Main|Equipment}}
'''Hepatizon equipment''' is [[Copper equipment|copper equipment]] upgraded with [[Hepatizon Alloy|hepatizon alloy]], a copper, silver and gold alloy. It has the fastest mining speeds in the pack, and every piece adds movement speed.

== Obtaining ==
Hepatizon alloy is crafted from seven copper ingots, a [[Silver Bullion|silver bullion]] and a gold ingot. Copper equipment is upgraded at a [[Smithing Table|smithing table]] with no template (a [[Smithing Upgrade Template|template]] for the dolabra and mattock). It is repaired with blocks of copper. See also the [[Hepatizon Laurel]] and [[Elytra#Hepatizon Elytra|hepatizon elytra]].

== Characteristics ==
Pickaxe, axe, shovel and hoe mine at speed 20, faster than adamant (15); the 1.12.1-alpha notes say the buff was "to make it worth using after obtaining Adamant". Each armor piece adds 0.01 movement speed (10% of the base 0.1), so the full set adds 40%. The sword has [[Riposte]] II and the spear Lunge III.

The video describes hepatizon as "a gold-silver-copper alloy that has high base mining speed and when worn, makes you run faster."<ref>{{Cite video|quote=Hepatizon, a gold-silver-copper alloy that has high base mining speed and when worn, makes you run faster.}}</ref>

== History ==
{{History|
{{History line|0.4-alpha|The spear (then "bronze spear") was buffed to Lunge III.}}
{{History line|1.10|Hepatizon was renamed from "Bronze" in the language file only, so existing items keep working. Buffed hepatizon equipment.}}
{{History line|1.12|The spear's real attack speed now matches its tooltip.}}
{{History line|1.12.1-alpha|Mining speed raised from about 13 to 20, so that hepatizon stays useful after adamant. Mattock and dolabra mining speed raised from about 12 to 15.}}
{{History line|1.12.2|Dolabras were redefined as axe (tool) and pickaxe hybrids rather than weapons: damage goes down and weapon intrinsics are removed over time.}}
}}

== Trivia ==
* Hepatizon was called "Bronze" until 1.10; internal IDs such as the alloy recipe <code>bronze_alloy</code> keep the old name. The developer still calls it bronze in the video.
